facts_replacements.F3:
[F3] [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]: for real $f$, the field is symmetric
and essentially self-adjoint on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$; its
self-adjoint closure is the closed Segal-field generator at
$\sqrt2K_\mu f$, and the field on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ is its
restriction.
facts_replacements.F4:
[F4] [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]: the vacuum two-point function is
$\langle K_\mu\overline f,K_\mu g\rangle_2$. For complex $f$,
conjugating the first test gives the nonnegative value
$\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(\overline f)\Phi_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle=\|K_\mu f\|_2^2$;
for real $f$ the ordinary diagonal $g=f$ has this same nonnegative value.

exact_supplier_statement_quotes.F3:
This is a complex-linear map of test functions into operators
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\to\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For real $f$ it is symmetric
and equals $\sqrt2\,\Phi_{\rm Segal}(K_\mu f)|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}$, where the Segal field of
[[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]] is
$\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=\overline{(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2}$.
exact_supplier_statement_quotes.F4:
The vacuum has zero one-point function and
two-point function
$$\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(f)\Phi_\mu(g)\Omega\rangle_2 =\langle K_\mu\overline f,K_\mu g\rangle_2,$$
which obeys $\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(\overline f)\Phi_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2=\|K_\mu f\|_2^2\ge0$ for every complex test $f$ (ordinary diagonal positivity holds for real tests);
